note: Curated factual summaries, not copied museum/article prose. Date envelopes are explicit broad filtering bins, not statistical confidence intervals. Coordinates are selected from the accompanying CC0 snapshot and rounded to two decimal places.

records.name: Oseberg
records.context: A vessel used as the burial ship for two women, not a sea wreck.
records.locationNote: Original Oseberg burial mound near Tønsberg. The ship entity's Oslo museum coordinate is deliberately not used.

records.name: Gokstad
records.dateBasis: Approximate burial date; filter uses nominal year, not an invented uncertainty interval
records.context: An ocean-going Viking ship later used for an elite burial.
records.locationNote: Original Gokstad Mound near Sandefjord, not the ship's modern museum.

records.name: Tune
records.dateBasis: Approximate burial date; filter uses nominal year, not an invented uncertainty interval
records.context: A ship burial beside the Glomma River at Rolvsøy. The date describes burial, not construction.
records.locationNote: The reviewed Rolvsøy claim is used. The separate Oslo museum coordinate on the same Wikidata entity is excluded.

records.name: Ladby
records.context: A Viking ship burial on Funen; the remains are preserved at their discovery site.
records.locationNote: Ladby burial site, not a relocated display ship.

records.name: Skuldelev ships (5)
records.dateBasis: Deliberate sinking; broad century filter envelope
records.context: Five vessels deliberately sunk in successive phases to form a barrier in Roskilde Fjord. Shown as one find-site record, not five separate locations.
records.locationNote: Peberrenden find area near Skuldelev, north of Roskilde; not the museum in Roskilde.

records.name: Hedeby 1
records.context: A longship recovered from Hedeby harbour, interpreted as a fire ship used in an attack—not a vessel lost in an ordinary storm.
records.locationNote: Locality-level coordinate for historic Hedeby and its harbour area, not an exact excavation fix. The ship's museum-area coordinate is not used.

records.name: Kyrenia
records.context: A Greek/Hellenistic-associated merchant ship. Published sinking estimates differ; cultural association is not proof of the crew's identity.
records.locationNote: Reported find area off Kyrenia, not the castle museum. Regional mapping only.

records.name: Antikythera
records.context: A Roman-era wreck with Greek artworks and the Antikythera mechanism. Roman-era describes chronology, not a proven crew nationality.
records.locationNote: Reported wreck area off Antikythera, not the museum holding its finds.

records.name: Mahdia
records.context: A Roman-period wreck off Tunisia with a cargo of Greek art and architectural pieces.
records.locationNote: Reported offshore find area near Mahdia; approximate, not a diving fix.

records.name: Madrague de Giens
records.context: A large Roman merchant vessel excavated off the Giens peninsula in southern France.
records.locationNote: Reported wreck area at La Madrague de Giens. Approximate coastal mapping only.

records.name: Mazarrón ships (2)
records.context: Two Phoenician ship finds grouped at one site. This group replaces the background Mazarron 1 record; it is not counted twice.
records.locationNote: Approximate find area at Mazarrón. The Oxford-derived point differs; no location is presented as a surveyed wreck fix.

records.name: Bajo de la Campana
records.context: A Phoenician-associated trading vessel at a reef off southeastern Spain. Its identification is archaeological, not a modern national flag.
records.locationNote: Reported reef/find area near La Manga; approximate regional placement only.

records.name: Uluburun
records.context: A Late Bronze Age trading ship with a diverse cargo. It is not automatically labelled Phoenician or Greek; origin and crew identity remain uncertain.
records.locationNote: Reported find area south of Kaş. Regional placement, not a precise wreck-site guide.

records.name: Nemi ships (2)
records.dateBasis: Construction/use under Caligula, not an established sinking date
records.context: Two Roman lake vessels built under Caligula, grouped as one Lake Nemi find-site record. Recovered in 1929–1932 and destroyed by fire in 1944. These were inland lake ships, not Mediterranean sea wrecks; the date describes construction/use, not their sinking.
records.locationNote: Lake-level anchor for Lake Nemi, not the modern museum or either vessel's exact lake-bed position.

records.name: Vasa
records.dateBasis: Sinking on the maiden voyage, 10 August 1628
records.context: The Swedish warship sank in Stockholm harbour on her maiden voyage and was recovered in 1961. This is an early-modern vessel, not a Viking ship.
records.locationNote: Coarse Beckholmen-area anchor near the documented original sinking/find location. Not the current Vasa Museum and not an exact seabed fix.

records.name: Mary Rose
records.dateBasis: Sinking during the Battle of the Solent, 19 July 1545
records.context: Henry VIII's warship sank in the Solent after decades of service. The surviving hull was raised in 1982; it was not lost on its maiden voyage.
records.locationNote: Original protected wreck-site polygon centroid from Historic England via the licensed EMODnet product, rounded for regional display. The Portsmouth museum coordinate on Wikidata is deliberately excluded.

records.name: Kronan
records.dateBasis: Sinking at the Battle of Öland, 1 June 1676
records.context: The Swedish flagship capsized and exploded during the Battle of Öland. Its wreck was rediscovered in 1980; recovered finds are displayed in Kalmar.
records.locationNote: Reported offshore wreck area east of Öland, not the Kalmar museum containing recovered objects.

records.name: Gribshunden
records.context: A Danish royal flagship lost near Ronneby in 1495. The late-medieval wreck is important evidence for early carvel-built warships; it is not a Viking longship.
records.locationNote: Reported wreck area near Stora Ekön in the Ronneby archipelago, not the Blekinge Museum.

records.name: Bremen cog
records.dateBasis: Dendrochronological timber/construction date; exact sinking year not established
records.context: A medieval cargo vessel found during Weser dredging in 1962, probably lost before construction was finished. The 1380 date comes from its timbers, not an independently established exact sinking year.
records.locationNote: Locality-level Rablinghausen anchor for the documented Weser find area, not an exact excavation fix. The current museum in Bremerhaven is far downstream and is not plotted.
